_comment: The automatic money cap, as ONE rule, pinned from both languages.
In automatic mode the trader states a percentage of the account and the
engine turns it into a currency cap for the next ticket:
pct = clamp(typed, risk_pct_min, risk_pct_max)
pct = min(pct, risk_pct_cap)        # only when a prop ceiling is armed
cap = round_half_up(equity * pct / 100, 2)
The desk draws a preview of this while the trader is still typing, so the
rule is evaluated in two languages and the two must not drift. Python:
aurion.runtime.risk.auto_risk_cap. JavaScript: autoRiskCap in app.js.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The desk used to reuse risk_pct_effective - the
already-resolved answer for the SAVED percentage - as if it were a
ceiling on the percentage being typed. It is not a ceiling, it is an
answer, so the preview was frozen at the saved value: on 10,000 equity
with 1% saved, typing 3% still previewed 100 while the engine would
apply 300. Wrong in every case where a preview is worth drawing.
The engine now publishes the rule's INPUTS (min, max, prop ceiling) and
both sides run the same arithmetic over them.
ROUNDING IS PART OF THE RULE, not a detail of the host language.
Python's round() is half-to-even and JavaScript's Math.round() is
half-up, so they disagree by a cent on a cap like 2250 x 0.05% = 1.125.
Half-up is what a trader reading the percentage expects, so half-up is
the rule and both sides implement it explicitly. C# will have to as
well - Math.Round is half-to-even there too.
Adding a case here is how the rule changes, and it must then pass on
both sides.

cases.why: the plain case: 1% of a 10,000 account
typing a bigger number must move the preview - this is the bug
typing a smaller number must move it too
above the ceiling the engine holds at the maximum, not at what was typed
below the floor it is lifted to the minimum, so the preview must lift too
a prop ceiling lowers the percentage
a prop ceiling never RAISES it - the tighter of the two wins
the real FTMO-style 0.40% ceiling against a desk asking for 2%
both ceilings at once - the maximum first, then the prop one
half-up at the half-cent: half-to-even would answer 1.12
an ordinary fractional cap, rounded to the cent
no equity reported yet - the rule has nothing to size against
a negative equity is not a negative cap
nothing typed yet reads as the floor, never as no rule at all
a small account still gets a cent-accurate cap
